::: {.section-intro}
lmmix fits Gaussian linear mixed models by maximum likelihood or REML. Its main use case combines random effects with structured residual covariance.
:::

GitHub development version: 0.4.0. Not distributed on CRAN.

::: {.link-list}
[GitHub](https://github.com/AurelienNicosiaULaval/lmmix){.btn .btn-outline-dark}
[Documentation](https://aureliennicosiaulaval.github.io/lmmix/){.btn .btn-outline-dark}
:::

## Models and inference

The package supports independent, compound-symmetric, AR(1), Toeplitz and unstructured residual covariance. It includes Satterthwaite and Kenward-Roger inference, model comparisons and estimated marginal means.

## Scope and validation

The [validation vignette](https://aureliennicosiaulaval.github.io/lmmix/articles/validation.html) documents comparisons with independent R implementations and PROC MIXED examples, including tolerances and limitations.

The current scope is univariate Gaussian responses. Some covariance matrices and inference calculations remain dense, so large-scale computation depends on the model structure.

Public sources checked on September 23, 2026.
